biggest_gap.title: On A4 paper the print layout base breaks e-mail addresses and date-times in the middle, most visibly in Arabic
biggest_gap.detail: Every report will build on this print base: invoices, delivery notes and statements a UAE trading company hands to customers. On the A4 printout of the users list, the e-mail column breaks addresses at any character, for example 'lang.tester@alnoor.ex' then 'ample', or 'rahul.reyes.100000@a' then 'lnoor.example'. The last sign-in date-time is also split over two lines. In Arabic the RTL column order makes this worse, because the narrow Latin columns are squeezed beside wide Arabic text. Nothing is clipped or off the page (print12.json: no header outside 718 px, no clipped cell), but a printed document with half-words in its addresses and dates looks unfinished. On a customer document the same break would cut a TRN, an IBAN or an invoice number. Fix: in the shared print stylesheet, never break inside identifier-like values (e-mail, codes, numbers, dates). Give such columns white-space: nowrap or break only at '@' and '.', size the columns from their content, and shrink or wrap the free-text columns instead. Add an e2e print check, in English and Arabic, that no e-mail or date cell renders on more than one line.
biggest_gap.evidence: In the demo (./erp up), sign in as admin.ar@alnoor.example. Press G then U, open the third row, then print to A4 (or emulate print media at 718 px width). drivers/print12.mjs writes print-users-ar-a4.pdf, print-user-record-ar-a4.pdf and print-users-en-a4.pdf. 09-print-a4-record-then-list-ar.jpg shows the record printed first, then the list with broken e-mails such as 'lang.tester@alnoor.ex / ample' and split date-times in the 'آخر تسجيل دخول' column.

other_findings: Round 12 gaps FIXED and holding. The browser G1 journey now runs Alt+L, the language button, the digits action, My preferences and the navigation pane while B's record is open, and judges every device key's value against the reviewed shapes in tests/Gates/device-keys.txt; CL3b re-applied unchanged is caught. The help sheet now has a forms section (Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Enter, Alt+Z, Alt+PgDn/PgUp, Alt+R, Esc, Alt+O; help12.json). With a record open, 'Print this screen' now prints the record first and the list after it (09 screenshot). The one-command verify, which failed in round 12 on a load-dependent harness test, passed this time at a peak load of 34.

SL3 (the preferences answer falls back to the Arabic display name last saved by any caller, kept in a static) was caught only by the static process-state gate. The runtime checks G1NonInterference (7 m 48 s) and the 3 G1ShellAnswers tests passed on it, likely because no tenant user in their scenarios has an empty Arabic name. The gate suite as a whole holds. Running a turn where the judged tenant's user has no Arabic display name would make the runtime checks see this kind of fallback too.
The modelled human margin on reach-screen-keyboard is still thin: 3.66 s against 3.99 s. Every count metric wins clearly, and machine seconds are about 5 times better.

Positive: the sign-in screen is right to left under an ar-AE locale, with the e-mail field focused and a font stack led by Noto Sans Arabic Variable. After sign-in the focus is on main. G then R lands in the list search box, Enter on a row focuses the record's first field, and Esc returns the focus to the grid. In both languages the palette finds sign out, print, language, digits and shortcuts (keyboard12.json). The digits switch renders the count as '١٠٠٬٠٠٦ مستخدمين' (shots13.json). Under print media the focused control has no outline (round 10's gap stays fixed).

Plants I wrote this round were plain, single-cause faults (CP1, SP4, SL3) plus the round 12 regression CL3b. I did not try plants that hide data inside a device key's allowed value shape. The device keys' allowed shapes still leave room for content the gates cannot tell from a real setting: erp.signInDomains accepts any 32 hex digits plus up to eight 16-hex-digit hashes. The owning builder may want to check, in the gate, that the hashes are derived from the domains actually signed in with. I did not test this myself.
Note: axe-core (MPL-2.0) was used only as a critic-side test tool from my scratchpad. It is not a product dependency.
